summary: Builds a sockaddr_in structure in the caller-provided buffer a3 from a host string and a port. Writes address family 2 (AF_INET), the port in network byte order via htons, and the binary IP address. Tries inet_addr first; on failure falls back to gethostbyname DNS resolution unless the host string is the broadcast literal '255.255.255.255'. Optionally reports the resolved result through output pointer a4.

local_names.a4: optional output pointer for the resolved address/host entry

operations.description: Set address-family field at the start of the a3 buffer to 2 (AF_INET)
Set port field at offset 2 to htons(hostshort), converting to network byte order
If host string cp is non-null, resolve the IP with inet_addr; otherwise write 0 (INADDR_ANY) to the address field
Write binary IP address at offset 4: inet_addr(cp) when cp is non-null, else 0
Accept the inet_addr result unless it equals -1 and the string is not the broadcast literal '255.255.255.255' (global a255255255255)
DNS fallback: call gethostbyname(cp); if it returns null, return that null result immediately; otherwise take the first address via the triple dereference at result + 12 and write it to offset 4
If output pointer a4 is non-null, store the resolved result through it (sockaddr buffer address on the inet_addr path, hostent pointer on the DNS path)
Return 1 on success; return 0 only when gethostbyname fails

unresolved: The value stored through a4 is the sockaddr buffer address when inet_addr succeeds but the hostent pointer when DNS resolution is used; the two types are inconsistent and the caller's expectation is unknown.
The buffer a3 is written without any length validation; the game trusts callers to provide a sockaddr_in-sized buffer.
The triple dereference at result + 12 is assumed to be h_addr_list[0]; the hostent layout is not validated in this function.
